spec.name: Graphics: Construction Site
spec.description: The construction site graphic shown while this building is being built. The game adds 110 to the value and uses the result as an entry in the Graphics lists below, where entries 116 to 126 are the construction sites; for example 6 (entry 116) is the land construction site and 15 (entry 125) the wall construction site. Frame 0 of the construction site is shown for the first quarter of the construction and frame 1 for the second quarter; after that the building's own graphic is used.
spec.values: Integer value between 0 and 16. Only used while the unit is being built.

spec.name: Graphics: General
spec.description: The graphic this unit uses on all tilesets. When the tileset's own Graphics list has an entry for the unit (not 0xFFFF), that one is used instead. Most units only set this one; buildings and the critter use the tileset-specific lists. Entries 0 to 109 are the units. Entries 110 to 126 are extra graphics: 110 and 111 are the peasant and peon carrying goods, 112 and 113 the peasant and peon carrying the other kind of goods, 114 and 115 the human and orc oil tanker carrying oil, and 116 to 126 (in the tileset lists) the construction sites (see Graphics: Construction Site).
spec.values: 0xFFFF means no graphic. Otherwise bits 0 to 14 are a file reference into the .war archives (the entry number plus 1000 for MAINDAT.WAR, so 1045 is entry 45 of MAINDAT.WAR).

bits.value: Reuse: instead of loading the graphic again, use the one already loaded for an earlier entry in the same list whose bits 0 to 14 are the same.

spec.name: Range: Sight
spec.description: Sight range (in tiles) of this unit: the unit reveals a square area of 2 × range + 1 tiles on each side around it. Rangers and Berserkers use 9 instead once their player has the sight upgrade (Scouting).
spec.values: Integer value between 0 and 9. The game uses the value as an entry in a table of 10 sight routines, so larger values are invalid. 0 works the same as 1.

spec.name: Hitpoints
spec.description: Hitpoints for this Unit.

spec.name: Magic Flag
spec.description: Copied into the unit's mana when the unit is created or changes type. It does not make the unit a spellcaster: whether a unit regains mana over time, and whether it starts with 85 mana, is decided by the Spellcaster bit (0x11) in Unit Flags.

spec.name: Cost: Build Time
spec.description: Time required to build or train this Unit. A higher value takes longer.

spec.name: Cost: Gold
spec.description: The amount of Gold required to build this Unit. Multiply by 10 to get actual value.

spec.name: Cost: Lumber
spec.description: Amount of Lumber required to build this Unit. Multiply by 10 to obtain actual value.

spec.name: Cost: Oil
spec.description: Amount of oil required to build this unit. Multiply by 10 to obtain actual value.

spec.name: Size: Unit
spec.description: First two bytes are the X size (width), second two are the Y size (height).

spec.name: Size: Box
spec.description: First two bytes are the X size (width), second two are the Y size (height).

spec.name: Attack Range
spec.description: Maximum distance (in tiles) from which this unit can attack its target. Rangers and Berserkers get one more once their player has the range upgrade (Longbow / Lighter Axes).

spec.name: React Range: Computer AI
spec.description: How far (in tiles) a computer player's unit of this type looks for enemies to attack.

spec.name: React Range: Human AI
spec.description: How far (in tiles) a human player's unit of this type looks for enemies to attack while it is walking somewhere, for example while patrolling. A human player's unit that is standing still only looks within its attack range.

spec.name: Armor
spec.description: Amount of armor this unit has.

spec.name: Multiselectable Flag
spec.description: Flag which determines whether the unit can be selected with other units.

spec.name: Priority / AI Treatment
spec.description: Used when a unit picks an enemy to attack by itself. Enemies that can attack come first (those within the unit's attack range before those further away), and among those the game picks the one with the highest priority minus a penalty for distance.

spec.name: Damage: Basic
spec.description: Basic damage dealt by this unit when it attacks.

spec.name: Damage: Piercing
spec.description: Piercing damage dealt by this unit when it attacks.

spec.name: Weapon Upgrade Flag
spec.description: Flag which determines whether this unit upgrades its weapon.

spec.name: Armor Upgrade Flag
spec.description: Flag which determines whether this unit upgrades its armor.

spec.name: Weapon Missile
spec.description: Missile this unit fires when it attacks. 0x1D (None) means the unit attacks in melee.

bits.value: Cannon Fire (shown at the unit that fires Cannon or Big Cannon)
Cannon Explosion (shown where Cannon or Big Cannon hits)

spec.name: Unit Type
spec.description: Whether the unit is a land, air or sea unit. Not only visual: the game copies it into each unit when the unit is created, and uses it, for example, when looking for a free square to place the unit on and when a missile hits the unit.

spec.name: Decay Rate
spec.description: How fast this unit decays. A unit with a non-zero decay rate gets a hidden timer that starts at 255. The game counts the decay rate down over and over; each time it runs out, the timer goes down by one and the unit's hit points are not affected. Once the timer reaches 0, the unit loses 5 hit points each time instead, and dies when it has fewer than 5 left. Decay rates only apply to units created during the game, not those placed on the map at design time, and never to units with the Spellcaster bit (0x11) in Unit Flags.
spec.values: Integer value between 0 and 255. 0 means the unit never decays.

spec.name: Repair Priority (Computer)
spec.description: How urgently a computer player repairs this building. When a computer player's peasant or peon looks for a building to repair, it considers its player's finished buildings in the same area that have less than 3/4 of their hit points, and picks the one with the highest value. This is the only place the game uses this field.
spec.values: Integer value between 0 and 255. Only matters for buildings.

spec.name: Right Click Action
spec.description: What this unit does when you have it selected and right click. The game turns the right click into an order depending on this value and on what was clicked.

bits.value: Attack: Attack an enemy unit, Attack Wall on a wall, otherwise Move. Units without the Attacks bit (0x13) in Unit Flags always Move
Harvest: Attack an enemy unit; Harvest a gold mine or trees when not carrying anything; Return with Goods to an own building that takes what is carried; Repair a damaged own building; otherwise Move
Haul Oil: Harvest an own oil platform when empty; Return with Goods to an own building that takes oil when carrying oil; otherwise Move
Demolish: Demolish an enemy unit, otherwise Move

spec.name: Point Value
spec.description: Point value awarded towards total score for a player which destroys this unit.

spec.name: Weapon Attack Domain
spec.description: Domain whose units this unit can attack.
spec.values: Bit flags; any combination is valid (just add them together). 0 means the unit cannot attack.

spec.name: Unit Flags
spec.description: Flags which determine special properties this unit has.

bits.value: Leaves no remains: when a unit with this bit is killed, it is removed straight away, instead of turning into a dead body (units) or leaving a destroyed site behind (buildings). Set on the dead body and the destroyed sites in the default data

Sapper; Set on the Dwarven Demolition Squad and Goblin Sappers in the default data; it does not make them explode (that is the Demolish order). The flag means it is Non-combatant: Like Peon (0x08), Tanker (0x09) and Mage (0x1A): when attacked, the unit moves away instead of fighting back; it does not come to help nearby friendly units that are attacked; computer players never pick it for an attack group; and when looking for enemies it plans its path around enemy units instead of through them. The flag also gives the unit the same death sound as units with Exploding Death (0x02) and air units.

spec.name: Graphics: Swamp
spec.description: The graphic this unit uses on Swamp maps. 0xFFFF means the unit uses its Graphics: General entry on this tileset. Only present in the Beyond the Dark Portal format: with this field the UDTA data is 5948 bytes long, without it 5694 bytes (the PUD UDTA section is 2 bytes longer than that, because of the word in front of the data that tells whether the default data is used).
spec.values: 0xFFFF means no graphic. Otherwise bits 0 to 14 are a file reference into the .war archives (the entry number plus 1000 for MAINDAT.WAR, so 1045 is entry 45 of MAINDAT.WAR).

bits.value: Reuse: instead of loading the graphic again, use the one already loaded for an earlier entry in the same list whose bits 0 to 14 are the same.
